text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.
LONDON - British shares jumped, inspired by Wall Street's continuing advance and positive results from some large British companies. The FTSE 100 index rose 22.8 points to 4,327.1.
FRANKFURT - The German DAX index rose to another record, continuing its strong run of recent weeks. The DAX-30 index rose 13.34 points to 3,229.48.

PARIS - French shares also hit a record high, underpinned by the rising dollar and further gains on Wall Street. A weaker franc vs. the dollar would make French exports more competitive. The blue-chip CAC-40 index added 29.08 points to 2,628.41.

ZURICH - The Swiss market's 10-day run of record highs ended as profit taking pulled shares lower. Dealers welcomed the correction, saying it was not expected to dampen overall sentiment. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) slipped 1.95 points to 2,824.34.

TOKYO - Stocks rallied for the third straight day, inspired by the weak yen which supported blue-chip issues and Wall Street's strength. The Nikkei average of leading 225 issues finished up 278.10 points or 1.5 percent at 18,688.06.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks tumbled as stock index futures plummeted and worries remerged about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping. The Hang Seng Index fell 222.66 points or 1.65 percent to 13,239.95.

SYDNEY - A confident Australian share market smashed records to close higher with traders in an upbeat mood as big banks and miners showed the way up. The All Ordinaries index jumped 22.9 points to 2,496.4.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares rose in hectic trading. The all-share index rose 75.1 points to 7,041.5, the industrial index added 70 points to 8,332.8 and the gold index rose 40.3 points to 1,390.40.
